fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents accurately present an applied data scientist with operational modelling, evaluation, SQL/dbt and limited Google Cloud exposure. They do not turn four-plus years of data science into four-plus years of production ML engineering, and the letter explicitly describes the career transition. However, the central gaps in assistants/RAG, serving, monitoring, MLOps, deployment and software delivery remain largely unaddressed; the CV also omits the explicit transition statement that appears in the letter.

issues: The summary is repetitive: 'Experienced in building forecasting and churn models' is followed by 'Experienced in developing applied machine learning models' describing the same background.
The summary does not explain the move into ML engineering, although the source CV and final letter do.
The food-waste estimate qualifier is less clear than in the source: use 'reduced food waste by an estimated 9%'.
The document is credible and well structured, but it cannot establish the required production ML engineering tenure.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts in a sensible order, with intact words, standard headings and clear employment dates.

Python, feature engineering, Google Cloud through BigQuery, Git and model evaluation are represented; evaluation is expressed through holdout validation and forecast metrics rather than the exact phrase.
The required four years of production ML engineering are not established by the Data Scientist title or the work described.
Most specialist support-AI and production MLOps keywords are absent because the candidate material does not substantiate them; they should not be added as claimed skills.

issues: Company specificity comes principally from the advertised merchant-support use case; the letter makes little use of the supplied ownership, feedback or learning-culture information.
The letter repeats much of the CV rather than explaining a particularly strong bridge from the candidate's experience to support-AI engineering.
It acknowledges the move into ML engineering but does not directly distinguish operational use of models from deployment, serving and operating production ML systems.
The phrase 'reduced forecast error from 23% to 14% and estimated food waste by 9%' places the estimate qualifier awkwardly.
strengths: Names the correct company, role and Customer Support AI team.
Uses concrete, supported modelling outcomes and evaluation methods.
Honestly describes the candidate as moving towards ML engineering rather than claiming the required engineering tenure.
Connects the application to models and assistants helping merchants and support agents.
Professional, concise and consistent with the CV.

culture_used: The letter refers to 'practical, team-based work described in the role', consistent with the advertised cross-functional collaboration and the company's team-first emphasis.

spacing_issues: The CV's skills section is relatively dense, with 'calendar features' wrapping onto a short continuation line.
Both documents leave substantial lower-page whitespace, particularly the letter; this is not an overflow or pagination problem.
consistency_issues: The CV uses a large centred name and centred contact block, whereas the letter uses a smaller left-aligned header. The shared serif typeface keeps the set reasonably coherent, but the header treatment is not fully matched.
issues: The CV's 10-point body and 9-point minimum text are readable but somewhat small; some of the spare page space could support a slightly more generous presentation.

fluency_and_tone_issues: CV: 'reducing WAPE from 23% to 14% and estimated food waste by 9%' would be clearer as 'reducing WAPE from 23% to 14% and food waste by an estimated 9%'.
Letter: 'The model reduced forecast error from 23% to 14% and estimated food waste by 9%' has the same misplaced estimate qualifier.
CV: 'Experienced in building...' and 'Experienced in developing...' repeat the same point within the summary.
Letter: 'a compelling application of that direction' is abstract and less natural than a direct explanation of interest in merchant-support AI.

evaluation.summary: Both documents are faithful to the candidate material, preserve the relevant achievements and avoid inventing production engineering or support-AI experience. The CV is clean, parseable and well organised, while the letter correctly targets Quillstone and honestly frames the move into ML engineering. The main limitation is the substantial mismatch with the required production ML tenure, assistants/RAG experience and MLOps capabilities, which the documents cannot substantiate. A less repetitive summary, clearer food-waste wording and a more specific explanation of transferable value would improve the application.
